09:00.headline: Close to home or best fit?
09:00.topic: Debate: a good-fit school near home vs. a better-fit school far away (hypothetical)

graphic.headline: Close to home or *best fit?*
graphic.sub: A hypothetical choice. Which way do you lean?

captions.instagram:
Close to home, or the best baseball fit?

Picture two hypothetical options for your son:
🅰️ A good fit 30 minutes away. You catch most home games, and he's close to family.
🅱️ A better fit 6 hours away. The level, coaching style and academics line up a little better, but you'll see far fewer games.

There's no wrong answer. Cost, his maturity, playing time and how he'll feel on a hard day all belong in the conversation.

captions.facebook:
The Baseball Parent Debate: close to home, or the best baseball fit?

Here's a hypothetical. Your son has two options:

A) A program that's a good fit, 30 minutes from home. You can make most home games and he's near family and friends.
B) A program that's a slightly better fit, 6 hours away. The level, coaching style and academics line up a little better, but you'd see far fewer games.

Both are good outcomes. The right answer depends on things only your family can weigh: total cost (including travel), how ready he is to be on his own, where he's likely to play, and whether he'd be happy at that school even if baseball ended tomorrow.

Parents who've already been through it: which did your family choose, and would you choose it again?

13:00.headline: Ask these 4 questions (before you pay for a showcase)

graphic.kicker: Before you pay for a showcase
graphic.headline: Ask these *4 questions*
items: Do the schools fit his level?

captions.instagram:
Showcase season is coming. Before you pay the entry fee, ask these 4 questions:

1️⃣ Which college coaches are actually expected to attend, and from which levels?
2️⃣ How many players are registered at his position?
3️⃣ Will his numbers (60, velo, exit velo, pop time) be measured and shared afterward?
4️⃣ Do the schools attending fit the levels on his target list?

The best showcase isn't always the biggest one. It's the one where the right coaches can see him.

Save this for the next registration email. 📌

Know where his numbers fit first: https://baseballfuture.com

captions.facebook:
Winter and spring showcase invites are starting to land in a lot of inboxes. Before you pay, a few questions worth asking the organizer:

✅ Which college coaches are expected to attend, and from which levels (D1, D2, D3, NAIA, JUCO)?
✅ How many players are registered at your son's position? More players can mean fewer reps in front of coaches.
✅ Will his numbers be measured and shared afterward, so he has something to send coaches?
✅ Do the attending schools line up with his realistic target list?

If the answers are vague, it may be worth putting that money toward a camp at a school he's genuinely interested in, or a better skills video.

(The 7.05 on our graphic is a sample reading, not a real player.)
